title: Phesgo + vinorelbine

agents.name: Pertuzumab
agents.mechanism: Blocks HER2 pairing with other receptors
agents.explanation: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway.
agents.watch: Keep heart-scan appointments. Report diarrhoea, new breathlessness, swelling or a treatment reaction.

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Keep heart-scan appointments. Report diarrhoea, new breathlessness, swelling or a treatment reaction.

agents.name: Vinorelbine
agents.explanation: Vinorelbine interferes with the microtubules that cells use to divide. It can also affect blood cells, nerves and bowel movement. The IV and oral doses are different; your prescription specifies one route.
agents.watch: Report new or worsening symptoms promptly and follow the agreed contact plan.
risks: Nausea; oral doses need a specific plan
Irritation if an IV dose leaks

phases_title: The phases and how they connect
phases_note: Relative sequence, not equal lengths or booked dates. Your team confirms actual appointments and the active medicines.
timeline_note: Treatment markers show the planned schedule. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves; serious symptoms can occur at any time.
safety_note: Serious symptoms need assessment on any day, even if the chart shows a usual recovery period.
teachback: Which medicines are active now, which days do you receive or take them, and who is booking and reviewing your next tests?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, common and serious effects, fertility and pregnancy precautions, route, monitoring, practical support and the agreed contact plan. The treating team completes the approved individual consent process.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, jaundice, unusual bleeding or sudden illness promptly. Do not wait for the next planned test.

support.title: Route-specific support
support.text: Oral vinorelbine needs a separate nausea plan; do not copy an IV-only minimal-risk template. Confirm anti-sickness treatment, constipation prevention and blood checks before each prescribed dose.

support.title: Tests before treatment
support.text: FBC, kidney and liver profile at baseline and before every 21-day cycle. The team reviews the necessary results before a planned dose. Confirm the blood-count check needed before each additional vinorelbine or paclitaxel dose; a Day 1 result does not automatically authorise a later dose. For oral vinorelbine, the product information requires blood counts on the day of each administration, including Day 8; the regimen source lists full blood/renal/liver checks before each cycle.

support.title: Keep heart checks on the plan
support.text: An echo every 12 weeks is separate from blood tests or cancer imaging. Ask who books and reviews it.

support.title: Plan for symptoms
support.text: Keep your agreed contact numbers and instructions. New symptoms can need assessment before a routine appointment.

questions.a: Ask the team who books each test, who checks the result and who to contact if an appointment is overdue. This map does not book appointments.

questions.q: What if I become unwell between visits?
questions.a: Use the urgent contact plan for sudden illness, fever, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea or poor fluid intake. Do not wait for a scheduled blood test or scan.

This NCCP option is for HER2-positive metastatic or unresectable locally recurrent cancer when taxane chemotherapy is clinically unsuitable and no chemotherapy or HER2 treatment has yet been given for metastatic disease. Phesgo combines two HER2 antibodies in one thigh injection. Vinorelbine provides a different chemotherapy option; its route and side effects need a separate discussion.

questions.q: When is my next heart scan?
questions.a: Check heart pumping function before starting HER2 treatment. Repeat echo or MUGA every 12 weeks: around cycle 5, then cycle 9 if 21-day cycles stay on time. Earlier checks are needed for symptoms or abnormal findings. Count elapsed time from the first HER2 dose; changing phase or route does not restart the clock. After the first year, ESC guidance allows six-monthly echo in selected asymptomatic low- or moderate-risk metastatic patients with normal assessments, only under an agreed team plan. Entering maintenance alone does not justify reducing checks.

Surgery or radiotherapy may be used for particular symptoms or disease sites. There is no routine surgery-then-radiation sequence for this advanced-cancer regimen. The oncology and radiation teams agree any treatment pause or overlap.

questions.q: Do I need regular scans or markers?
questions.a: Record baseline disease sites. Response imaging is generally reviewed every 2–4 months under international guidance, adapted to symptoms, disease pace and treatment. The team selects the scan; this is not an automatic CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order for every patient. Tumour markers may support assessment in selected cases, but do not alone decide progression or a treatment change.

No. This regimen uses vinorelbine on Days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle only, whether IV or oral. Oral vinorelbine is taken only on the prescribed Days 1 and 8, with some food. Swallow capsules whole with water; do not chew, suck, open or dissolve them. Do not use a damaged capsule. Do not take an extra dose after vomiting; contact the team. Dose increases require a new prescription and blood-count review.

items.text: Staff give this through a checked IV line. Tell them immediately about pain, burning or swelling. It must not be self-injected.

items.title: A bowel plan
items.text: Vinorelbine may slow bowel movement. Discuss prevention, any prescribed laxative and when to call; severe pain with vomiting or no stool/wind needs urgent assessment.

items.text: If the cancer is also hormone-receptor positive, endocrine treatment may form part of the wider plan. Bone-density testing is linked to aromatase inhibitors, ovarian suppression and fracture risk; it is not automatically required because a HER2 medicine is prescribed. Agree baseline DEXA where indicated and individual follow-up.

steps.title: Before the visit
steps.text: Confirm blood results, cardiac checks, active phase, previous dual HER2 dose and the consent discussion.

steps.title: The thigh injection
steps.text: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.

steps.title: Chemotherapy and access
steps.text: After Phesgo observation, receive the prescribed IV vinorelbine or follow the separately agreed oral dose plan. Phesgo itself needs no IV line; the oral vinorelbine option also avoids an infusion. IV vinorelbine still needs a cannula, PICC or port. No take-home infusion pump is routinely used.

steps.title: Leaving the unit
steps.text: Confirm supportive medicines, next visits and due tests. Injection time is shorter than the whole appointment; preparation, assessment and observation still take time.

details.title: Switching / a missed appointment
details.text: The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.
